senses.gloss: Amitra-tapana Śuṣmiṇa Śaibya is the name of him who killed Atyarāti jānaṃtapi, according to the aitareya brāhmaṇa (viii. 23).

Āmikṣā designates a mess of clotted curds. It is not known to the Rigveda, but occurs in all the later Saṃhitās, Brāhmaṇas, etc., and is associated with the vaiśya in the taittirīya Āraṇyaka.
Foot notes Av. x. 9, 13; taittirīya Saṃhitā, ii. 5, 5, 4; iii. 3, 9, 2; vi. 2, 5, 3; Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā, ii. 1, 9; Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xix. 21; 23, etc.
Satapatha brāhmaṇa, i. 8, 1, 7. 9; iii. 3, 3, 2, etc.; taittirīya Āraṇyaka, ii. 8, 8; Jaiminīya brāhmaṇa, ii. 438 (Journal of the American Oriental Society, 19, 99, 101); Chāndogya upaniṣad, viii. 8, 5, etc.
Loc. cit. Cf. mānava Srauta sūtra, ii. 2, 40.
